definitions.explanation: Used when making a modest, hesitant, or transitional statement.
An exclamation expressing surprise (often used by women).
Indicating something is acceptable but not exceptional.

notes:
まあ has several distinct uses that are told apart mainly by intonation and context. It is always written in kana.

HESITATION / SOFTENING (drawn-out, falling tone): softens a statement or turns firm agreement into a mild concession — "well…", "I guess". It typically opens a sentence, often before ⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧, ⟦そう→そう：01167_sou⟧, or a guess like ⟦だろう→だろう：09576_darou⟧, making the whole remark tentative rather than definite.

SURPRISE (short, rising tone): a standalone exclamation of mild surprise or admiration — "oh my!", "oh dear!". This use is traditionally feminine and now sounds somewhat old-fashioned. It comes before the thing noticed (まあ、⟦{素敵|すてき}→素敵：02356_suteki⟧！).

MODERATE DEGREE (reduplicated まあまあ): means "so-so, passable" — neither good nor bad. Used on its own, before an adjective (まあまあ⟦{美味|おい}しい→美味しい：00740_oishii⟧), or as まあまあ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ + noun ("passable results").

CALMING (まあまあ、 said soothingly): the same reduplicated form used to calm someone — "there, there", "now, now" (まあまあ、⟦{落|お}ち{着|つ}いて→落ち着く：04670_ochitsuku⟧).
